metadata.case_name: LIMBU PRYA v. HEI YUET PALACE RESTAURANT O/B KENBERG INVESTMENTS LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: kitchen helper/cleaner at the Defendant’s restaurant premises situated at Ground Floor (West Portion), 2nd-4th Floors, 267-275 Des Voeux Road Central, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong
plaintiff.occupation_after: employed as a part-time cleaner at a residential public housing block (3 hours per night, cleaning 2 lifts and the lift lobby) from 3.8.2006 to end of 2007; then part-time kitchen worker for about 4 to 5 months (paid $4,000 to $4,500 per month); subsequently gave up due to pain and limitation of movement

injuries.description: second degree burns all over her back and buttocks with blistering. Estimated body surface area involvement is about 18%
source: On 14.11.2005 her back was severely scalded by very hot water. On that day she went to the accident and emergency department at Queen Mary Hospital ("QMH"). She was examined by Dr. Wong Man Fung ("Dr. Wong") Dr. Wong found her to have second degree burns all over her back and buttocks with blistering. Estimated body surface area involvement is about 18%.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: areas of hypo-pigmented skin and at least one area of hyper-trophic scar on her back with pain on touching
source: On her back there are areas of hypo-pigmented skin and at least one area of hyper-trophic scar. She said that if she touches the area of her back with the hypo-pigmentation and hyper-trophic scar it is painful.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

manifestations.description: second degree burns all over her back and buttocks with blistering
areas of hypo-pigmented skin and at least one area of hyper-trophic scar on her back
pain at her back; painful when touching the hypopigmented and hyper-trophic scarred area
restrictions of the injured skin to normal movements
ability to tolerate full movements in order to work full-time (8 hours per day) might be hampered significantly by lack of rehabilitation support

treatments_received.treatment: attendance at Accident and Emergency department at Queen Mary Hospital
source: On that day she went to the accident and emergency department at Queen Mary Hospital ("QMH").

treatments_received.treatment: transfer from Queen Mary Hospital to Tung Wah Hospital (inpatient)
source: On 18.11.2005 she was transferred from QMH to the Tung Wah Hospital where she was discharged on 26.11.2005.

treatments_received.treatment: consultation/examination by Dr. Wong Man Fung (plastic surgery specialist)
source: She was examined by Dr. Wong Man Fung ("Dr. Wong") Dr. Wong found her to have second degree burns all over her back and buttocks with blistering.

treatments_received.treatment: consultation/examination by Dr. James Kong (specialist in plastic surgery)
source: She was examined by Dr. James Kong, a specialist in plastic surgery in July 2008. He found that the restrictions of the injured skin to normal movements were minimal and, her ability to tolerate full movements in order to work full-time (8 hours per day) might be hampered significantly by lack of rehabilitation support to her after the accident. In view of that he suggests that she undergo counselling and support.
The Plaintiff spent $1,825 on hospital charges.
Her total traveling expenses for attending hospitals was about $4,000.
In view of that he suggests that she undergo counselling and support.

losses.description: scarring and hypo-pigmentation with at least one hyper-trophic scar on back causing pain on touch and restriction of skin movement

comparable_cases.case_name: Leung Yuk Kwan v. Maple Professional Beauty Centre Limited
comparable_cases.injury_description: the Plaintiff’s right leg was “severely scalded” in the course of beauty treatment. She sought medical attention 3 days later, and first attended hospital 9 days later for treatment. One year later there an “ugly” scar on her right lower thigh. The size of the scar was about 4 x 5 cm. She suffered 3% cosmetic disability of the whole person. PSLA was awarded at $300,000.
